payload.label: Give an unknown sender a pairing code
payload.job: Hold a message from a sender the person has not paired yet and give that sender a short code the person can approve
payload.description: Give source_id (the event source the message came in on) and sender (the sender's own id on that source). Returns { paired: true } when the sender is already paired; otherwise code (8 characters with no 0, O, 1 or I), expires_at (an hour from now) and said. Asking again for the same sender gives the same code; a source with 3 codes waiting gives no more ({ full: true, said }). It reaches no database: give the pairing facts the person keeps as facts, and keep what the answer's keep lists.

facts.description: The pairing facts the person keeps, by name (pairing-waiting:<source>:<code> and pairing-paired:<source>:<sender>), read by the caller from wherever the person keeps them. Left out, none are kept yet.

keep.description: The facts this call wrote, to keep in the person's own database (the newest value per name is current)

payload.label: Approve a pairing code
payload.job: Let a waiting sender's messages through by approving the pairing code they were given
payload.description: Give code (case and spaces do not matter) and, optionally, source_id. A code works once, only before it expires, and only for the source it was issued for. Returns source_id, sender and said; an unknown, used or expired code is refused with what to do. It reaches no database: give the pairing facts the person keeps as facts, and keep what the answer's keep lists.

facts.description: The pairing facts the person keeps, by name (pairing-waiting:<source>:<code> and pairing-paired:<source>:<sender>), read by the caller from wherever the person keeps them. Left out, none are kept yet.

keep.description: The facts this call wrote, to keep in the person's own database (the newest value per name is current)

payload.label: Unpair a sender
payload.job: Stop letting a paired sender's messages through, so they are unknown again
payload.description: Give source_id and sender. The sender is no longer paired for that source; their next message gets a new code. Returns source_id, sender and said. It reaches no database: give the pairing facts the person keeps as facts, and keep what the answer's keep lists.

payload.label: Paired senders and waiting codes
payload.job: List which senders are paired and which pairing codes are waiting, for one source or all
payload.description: Optional source_id narrows to one source. With source_id and sender, also answers is_paired for that sender. Returns waiting [{ source_id, sender, code, expires_at }] (expired codes left out) and paired [{ source_id, sender, paired_at }]. It changes nothing. It reaches no database: give the pairing facts the person keeps as facts, and keep what the answer's keep lists.
